assessments.reasoning: The rendered paragraphs give the last-nonblank ampersand at line end or before a comment and require the next noncomment line's leading ampersand to adjoin the remaining characters of a split token.

challenge.method: Compare ordinary continuation, split tokens, character-context continuation and the standalone marker prohibition. Check the glyphs in render.
challenge.results: The leading marker is optional for ordinary noncharacter continuation. With a split token it must be first nonblank and immediately adjacent to the token remainder. Comments can intervene.

limitations: The leading-marker requirement in the claim applies to a split token. A line with only an ampersand remains disallowed under the separate first paragraph.
